sanskrit: yathā yathā naraḥ samyag adharmam anubhāṣate samāhitena manasā vimucyati tathā tathā bhujaṃga iva nirmokāt pūrvabhuktāj jarānvitāt
english: In the measure that a man, with a mind well composed, rightly acknowledges his own unrighteousness, in that same measure he is released from it, as a serpent slips free from the old, worn-out slough it once inhabited.

sanskrit: adattvāpi pradānāni vividhāni samāhitaḥ manaḥsamādhisaṃyuktaḥ sugatiṃ pratipadyate
english: Even without having bestowed gifts of various kinds, a man who is composed and joined to a steady concentration of mind attains a happy course hereafter.

sanskrit: pradānāni tu vakṣyāmi yāni dattvā yudhiṣṭhira naraḥ kṛtvāpy akāryāṇi tadā dharmeṇa yujyate
english: But I shall tell of those gifts, O Yudhiṣṭhira, by bestowing which a man, though he has done deeds that ought not to be done, is even then made one with righteousness.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva dānānām annaṃ śreṣṭham udāhṛtam pūrvam annaṃ pradātavyam ṛjunā dharmam icchatā
english: Of all gifts whatever, food is declared the most excellent; food first of all should be given by the upright man who desires righteousness.

sanskrit: prāṇā hy annaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tasmāj jantuś ca jāyate anne pratiṣṭhitā lokās tasmād annaṃ prakāśate
english: Food indeed is the very life-breath of men, and from it the living creature is born; the worlds are established upon food, and therefore food shines forth supreme.

sanskrit: annam eva praśaṃsanti devarṣipitṛmānavāḥ annasya hi pradānena svargam āpnoti kauśikaḥ
english: The gods, the sages, the ancestral fathers, and men all extol food alike; for by the gift of food a son of the Kuśika line attains heaven.

sanskrit: nyāyalabdhaṃ pradātavyaṃ dvijebhyo hy annam uttamam svādhyāyasamupetebhyaḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
english: Food obtained by lawful means should be given, the finest food, to the twice-born who are devoted to the recitation of the Veda, and given with an inmost self made glad.

sanskrit: yasya hy annam upāśnanti brāhmaṇānāṃ śatā daśa hṛṣṭena manasā dattaṃ na sa tiryaggatir bhavet
english: He upon whose food ten hundred brāhmaṇas feed, food given with a gladdened mind, shall never sink into the course of the beasts.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ sahasrāṇi daśa bhojya nararṣabha naro 'dharmāt pramucyeta pāpeṣv abhirataḥ sadā
english: Feeding ten thousand brāhmaṇas, O bull among men, a man, though ever given to sins, would be set free from unrighteousness.

sanskrit: bhaikṣeṇānnaṃ samāhṛtya vipro vedapuraskṛtaḥ svādhyāyanirate vipre dattveha sukham edhate
english: Having gathered food by begging, a brāhmaṇa who keeps the Veda foremost, and given it here to a brāhmaṇa intent upon his Vedic recitation, thrives in happiness.

sanskrit: ahiṃsan brāhmaṇaṃ nityaṃ nyāyena paripālya ca kṣatriyas tarasā prāptam annaṃ yo vai prayacchati
english: The kṣatriya who, never harming a brāhmaṇa and protecting his people by lawful rule, bestows food won by his own strength —

sanskrit: dvijebhyo vedavṛddhebhyaḥ prayataḥ susamāhitaḥ tenāpohati dharmātmā duṣkṛtaṃ karma pāṇḍava
english: — giving it to the twice-born grown ripe in the Veda, restrained and well composed, by that, O son of Pāṇḍu, the righteous soul wipes away his evil deeds.

sanskrit: ṣaḍbhāgapariśuddhaṃ ca kṛṣer bhāgam upārjitam vaiśyo dadad dvijātibhyaḥ pāpebhyaḥ parimucyate
english: And the vaiśya who gives to the twice-born the portion earned from his tillage, purified by the sixth part rendered to the king, is released from his sins.

sanskrit: avāpya prāṇasaṃdehaṃ kārkaśyena samārjitam annaṃ dattvā dvijātibhyaḥ śūdraḥ pāpāt pramucyate
english: Having amassed by harsh toil, at the very hazard of his life, the food he has earned, the śūdra who gives it to the twice-born is set free from sin.

sanskrit: aurasena balenānnam arjayitvāvihiṃsakaḥ yaḥ prayacchati viprebhyo na sa durgāṇi sevate
english: He who, doing harm to none, earns food by the strength of his own breast and bestows it upon the brāhmaṇas, never resorts to the realms of hardship.

sanskrit: nyāyenāvāptam annaṃ tu naro lobhavivarjitaḥ dvijebhyo vedavṛddhebhyo dattvā pāpāt pramucyate
english: But the man free from greed who, having won food by lawful means, gives it to the twice-born grown ripe in the Veda, is released from sin.

sanskrit: annam ūrjaskaraṃ loke dattvorjasvī bhaven naraḥ satāṃ panthānam āśritya sarvapāpāt pramucyate
english: Food is the giver of vigor in the world; giving it, a man becomes full of vigor, and treading the path of the good, he is freed from every sin.

sanskrit: dānakṛdbhiḥ kṛtaḥ panthā yena yānti manīṣiṇaḥ te sma prāṇasya dātāras tebhyo dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: A road has been laid down by those who make their gifts, along which the wise go their way; they are the givers of life itself, and from them flows the eternal righteousness.

sanskrit: sarvāvasthaṃ manuṣyeṇa nyāyenānnam upārjitam kāryaṃ pātragataṃ nityam annaṃ hi paramā gatiḥ
english: Food earned by lawful means should always, in every condition, be set by a man into a worthy vessel; for food is the supreme goal.

sanskrit: annasya hi pradānena naro durgaṃ na sevate tasmād annaṃ pradātavyam anyāyaparivarjitam
english: For by the giving of food a man does not resort to the realm of hardship; therefore food should be given, food untainted by unlawful gain.

sanskrit: yated brāhmaṇapūrvaṃ hi bhoktum annaṃ gṛhī sadā avandhyaṃ divasaṃ kuryād annadānena mānavaḥ
english: Let the householder ever strive to eat his food only after the brāhmaṇa has eaten first; thus by the gift of food let a man make no day of his barren.

sanskrit: bhojayitvā daśaśataṃ naro vedavidāṃ nṛpa nyāyaviddharmaviduṣām itihāsavidāṃ tathā
english: Feeding a thousand men who know the Veda, O king, who are versed in the law and in righteousness and likewise learned in the ancient lore —

sanskrit: na yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ saṃsārāṃś ca na sevate sarvakāmasamāyuktaḥ pretya cāpy aśnute phalam
english: — he does not go to the dreadful hell, nor does he resort to the rounds of rebirth; endowed with all desires fulfilled, he enjoys his reward even after death.

sanskrit: evaṃ sukhasamāyukto ramate vigatajvaraḥ rūpavān kīrtimāṃś caiva dhanavāṃś copapadyate
english: Thus joined to happiness he takes his delight, his fever gone; and he is born again comely of form, renowned, and rich in wealth.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātam annadānaphalaṃ mahat mūlam etad dhi dharmāṇāṃ pradānasya ca bhārata
english: All this great fruit of the gift of food has been declared to you; for this, O descendant of Bharata, is the root of all observances of dharma and of giving.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ahiṃsā vaidikaṃ karma dhyānam indriyasaṃyamaḥ tapo 'tha guruśuśrūṣā kiṃ śreyaḥ puruṣaṃ prati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Non-harming, the rites enjoined by the Veda, meditation, the restraint of the senses, austerity, and service to one's elders — which of these is best for a man?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca sarvāṇy etāni dharmasya pṛthag dvārāṇi sarvaśaḥ śṛṇu saṃkīrtyamānāni ṣaḍ eva bharatarṣabha
english: Bṛhaspati said: All these, every one, are separate gateways of dharma; hear them, O bull of the Bhāratas, all six as I proclaim them in full.

sanskrit: hanta niḥśreyasaṃ jantor ahaṃ vakṣyāmy anuttamam ahiṃsāpāśrayaṃ dharmaṃ yaḥ sādhayati vai naraḥ
english: Come, I shall declare the unsurpassed and highest good of every creature: the dharma that rests upon non-harming, which a man should indeed bring to fulfillment.

sanskrit: trīn doṣān sarvabhūteṣu nidhāya puruṣaḥ sadā kāmakrodhau ca saṃyamya tataḥ siddhim avāpnute
english: Laying aside ever the three faults toward all beings, and curbing both desire and wrath, a man thereby attains perfection.

sanskrit: ahiṃsakāni bhūtāni daṇḍena vinihanti yaḥ ātmanaḥ sukham anvicchan na sa pretya sukhī bhavet
english: He who, seeking his own happiness, strikes down with the rod creatures that do no harm, shall not be happy in the world to come.

sanskrit: ātmopamaś ca bhūteṣu yo vai bhavati pūruṣaḥ nyastadaṇḍo jitakrodhaḥ sa pretya sukham edhate
english: But the man who holds all beings as like unto himself, who has laid down the rod and conquered his wrath, thrives in happiness in the world to come.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtātmabhūtasya sarvabhūtāni paśyataḥ devāpi mārge muhyanti apadasya padaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Of him who has become the self of all beings, who beholds all beings as himself, even the gods lose the trail, as they seek the footprints of one who leaves no footprint.

sanskrit: na tat parasya saṃdadyāt pratikūlaṃ yad ātmanaḥ eṣa saṃkṣepato dharmaḥ kāmād anyaḥ pravartate
english: Let no man do to another what is hateful to himself; this, in brief, is dharma — all else proceeds from desire.

sanskrit: pratyākhyāne ca dāne ca sukhaduḥkhe priyāpriye ātmaupamyena puruṣaḥ samādhim adhigacchati
english: In refusal and in giving, in pleasure and pain, in what is dear and what is hateful, by measuring others against himself a man attains to inner harmony.

sanskrit: yathā paraḥ prakramate 'pareṣu; tathāparaḥ prakramate parasmin eṣaiva te 'stūpamā jīvaloke; yathā dharmo naipuṇenopadiṣṭaḥ
english: As one man behaves toward others, so will another behave toward him; let this be your measure in the world of the living, even as dharma has been skillfully taught to you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā taṃ suragurur dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram divam ācakrame dhīmān paśyatām eva nas tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of righteousness, the wise preceptor of the gods ascended to heaven, even as we looked on.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā śaratalpe pitāmaham punar eva mahātejāḥ papraccha vadatāṃ varam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira of great splendor once more questioned his grandsire, best of all who speak, where he lay upon his bed of arrows.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo brāhmaṇā devāḥ praśaṃsanti mahāmate ahiṃsālakṣaṇaṃ dharmaṃ vedaprāmāṇyadarśanāt
english: O greatly wise one, the sages, the brāhmaṇas, and the gods extol the dharma marked by non-harming, since they see the authority of the Veda for it.

sanskrit: karmaṇā manujaḥ kurvan hiṃsāṃ pārthivasattama vācā ca manasā caiva kathaṃ duḥkhāt pramucyate
english: O best of kings, a man who works harm by deed, by word, and by thought — how is he set free from sorrow?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca caturvidheyaṃ nirdiṣṭā ahiṃsā brahmavādibhiḥ eṣaikato 'pi vibhraṣṭā na bhavaty arisūdana
english: Bhīṣma said: This non-harming has been laid down as fourfold by those who expound the sacred word; O slayer of foes, if it falls away even on one side, it ceases to be.

sanskrit: yathā sarvaś catuṣpādas tribhiḥ pādair na tiṣṭhati tathaiveyaṃ mahīpāla procyate kāraṇais tribhiḥ
english: As any four-footed beast cannot stand upon three feet, so too, O lord of the earth, this is said to fail when held by only three of its grounds.

sanskrit: yathā nāgapade 'nyāni padāni padagāminām sarvāṇy evāpidhīyante padajātāni kauñjare evaṃ lokeṣv ahiṃsā tu nirdiṣṭā dharmataḥ parā
english: As in the elephant's footprint all other footprints of creatures that go on foot, every kind of footprint, are wholly contained, so in the worlds is non-harming declared the highest by the measure of dharma.

sanskrit: karmaṇā lipyate jantur vācā ca manasaiva ca
english: A creature is stained by deed, by word, and by thought alone.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ tu manasā tyaktvā tathā vācātha karmaṇā trikāraṇaṃ tu nirdiṣṭaṃ śrūyate brahmavādibhiḥ
english: But first renouncing harm in thought, then in word, then in deed — this threefold ground is laid down and is heard so taught by the expounders of the sacred word.

sanskrit: manovāci tathāsvāde doṣā hy eṣu pratiṣṭhitāḥ na bhakṣayanty ato māṃsaṃ tapoyuktā manīṣiṇaḥ
english: In the mind, in speech, and likewise in the relish of taste — in these the faults are seated; and therefore the wise who are given to austerity do not eat flesh.

sanskrit: doṣāṃs tu bhakṣaṇe rājan māṃsasyeha nibodha me putramāṃsopamaṃ jānan khādate yo vicetanaḥ
english: But hear from me, O king, the faults in the eating of flesh here below: it is a man bereft of sense who eats it, knowing it to be like the flesh of his own son.

sanskrit: mātāpitṛsamāyoge putratvaṃ jāyate yathā rasaṃ ca prati jihvāyāḥ prajñānaṃ jāyate tathā tathā śāstreṣu niyataṃ rāgo hy āsvāditād bhavet
english: As sonship is born from the union of mother and father, and as awareness of taste is born to the tongue, so too, it is settled in the scriptures, craving arises from the savoring.

sanskrit: asaṃskṛtāḥ saṃskṛtāś ca lavaṇālavaṇās tathā prajñāyante yathā bhāvās tathā cittaṃ nirudhyate
english: Unseasoned and seasoned, salted and saltless — according as such flavors are discerned, so is the mind bound fast to them.

sanskrit: bherīśaṅkhamṛdaṅgādyāṃs tantrīśabdāṃś ca puṣkalān niṣeviṣyanti vai mandā māṃsabhakṣāḥ kathaṃ narāḥ
english: How shall dull men who feed on flesh deserve to enjoy the abundant sounds of the kettledrum, the conch, the tabor, and the strings?

sanskrit: acintitam anuddiṣṭam asaṃkalpitam eva ca rasaṃ gṛddhyābhibhūtā vai praśaṃsanti phalārthinaḥ praśaṃsā hy eva māṃsasya doṣakarmaphalānvitā
english: Overcome by greed for its taste, those who seek a reward praise flesh — a thing unthought-of, unprescribed, and unintended; yet the very praise of flesh is bound up with the fruit of sinful deeds.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ hi parityajya bahavaḥ sādhavo janāḥ svamāṃsaiḥ paramāṃsāni paripālya divaṃ gatāḥ
english: For many good men, casting aside their very lives, have gone to heaven by shielding the flesh of others with their own flesh.

sanskrit: evam eṣā mahārāja caturbhiḥ kāraṇair vṛtā ahiṃsā tava nirdiṣṭā sarvadharmārthasaṃhitā
english: Thus, O great king, this non-harming, encompassed by its four grounds, has been laid down for you, containing within it the whole aim and meaning of dharma.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ahiṃsā paramo dharma ity uktaṃ bahuśas tvayā śrāddheṣu ca bhavān āha pitṝn āmiṣakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Non-harming is the highest dharma — so you have said many times; and yet at the rites for the dead you have said that the ancestral fathers long for flesh.

sanskrit: māṃsair bahuvidhaiḥ proktas tvayā śrāddhavidhiḥ purā ahatvā ca kuto māṃsam evam etad virudhyate
english: Long ago you set forth the rule of the funeral rite with flesh of many kinds; yet without slaying, whence comes flesh? In this way these teachings stand at odds.

sanskrit: jāto naḥ saṃśayo dharme māṃsasya parivarjane doṣo bhakṣayataḥ kaḥ syāt kaś cābhakṣayato guṇaḥ
english: A doubt has arisen in us concerning the dharma of abstaining from flesh: what fault would there be in one who eats it, and what merit in one who does not?

sanskrit: hatvā bhakṣayato vāpi pareṇopahṛtasya vā hanyād vā yaḥ parasyārthe krītvā vā bhakṣayen naraḥ
english: Whether a man slays and then eats, or eats what another has brought, or slays for another's sake, or buys and eats —

sanskrit: etad icchāmi tattvena kathyamānaṃ tvayānagha niścayena cikīrṣāmi dharmam etaṃ sanātanam
english: — this I wish to have told to me in its very truth by you, O sinless one; with sure resolve I desire to follow out this eternal dharma.

sanskrit: katham āyur avāpnoti kathaṃ bhavati sattvavān katham avyaṅgatām eti lakṣaṇyo jāyate katham
english: How does a man attain long life? How does he become full of vigor? How does he come to be free of any defect, and how is he born marked with auspicious signs?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca māṃsasya bhakṣaṇe rājan yo 'dharmaḥ kurupuṃgava taṃ me śṛṇu yathātattvaṃ yaś cāsya vidhir uttamaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: O king, O bull of the Kurus, hear from me, even as it truly is, the unrighteousness that lies in the eating of flesh, and what is the highest rule concerning it.

sanskrit: rūpam avyaṅgatām āyur buddhiṃ sattvaṃ balaṃ smṛtim prāptukāmair narair hiṃsā varjitā vai kṛtātmabhiḥ
english: Men of perfected souls, desiring to win beauty, soundness of body, long life, understanding, vigor, strength, and memory, have indeed renounced all harming.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇām atra saṃvādo bahuśaḥ kurupuṃgava babhūva teṣāṃ tu mataṃ yat tac chṛṇu yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this matter there has been much discourse among the sages, O bull of the Kurus; hear, O Yudhiṣṭhira, what their settled opinion is.

sanskrit: yo yajetāśvamedhena māsi māsi yatavrataḥ varjayen madhu māṃsaṃ ca samam etad yudhiṣṭhira
english: He who, holding firm to his vows, should offer the horse-sacrifice month after month, and he who renounces wine and flesh — these two, O Yudhiṣṭhira, are reckoned equal.

sanskrit: saptarṣayo vālakhilyās tathaiva ca marīcipāḥ amāṃsabhakṣaṇaṃ rājan praśaṃsanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: The Seven Sages, the Vālakhilyas, and likewise the Marīcipas, the wise ones, all extol the eating of no flesh, O king.

sanskrit: na bhakṣayati yo māṃsaṃ na hanyān na ca ghātayet taṃ mitraṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt
english: He who eats no flesh, who neither slays nor causes to be slain — him Manu, son of the Self-Existent, declared the friend of all beings.

sanskrit: adhṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ viśvāsyaḥ sarvajantuṣu sādhūnāṃ saṃmato nityaṃ bhaven māṃsasya varjanāt
english: By abstaining from flesh a man becomes unassailable by all beings, trusted among all living creatures, and ever esteemed by the good.

sanskrit: svamāṃsaṃ paramāṃsena yo vardhayitum icchati nāradaḥ prāha dharmātmā niyataṃ so 'vasīdati
english: He who would make his own flesh grow by the flesh of another — the righteous-souled Nārada has declared that such a man assuredly comes to ruin.

sanskrit: dadāti yajate cāpi tapasvī ca bhavaty api madhumāṃsanivṛttyeti prāhaivaṃ sa bṛhaspatiḥ
english: By turning away from wine and flesh a man both gives and sacrifices and becomes one given to austerity — thus did Bṛhaspati declare it.

sanskrit: māsi māsy aśvamedhena yo yajeta śataṃ samāḥ na khādati ca yo māṃsaṃ samam etan mataṃ mama
english: He who should offer the horse-sacrifice month after month for a hundred years, and he who eats no flesh — these two I hold to be equal.

sanskrit: sadā yajati satreṇa sadā dānaṃ prayacchati sadā tapasvī bhavati madhumāṃsasya varjanāt
english: By abstaining from wine and flesh a man ever offers the long sacrificial session, ever bestows gifts, and is ever one given to austerity.

sanskrit: sarve vedā na tat kuryuḥ sarvayajñāś ca bhārata yo bhakṣayitvā māṃsāni paścād api nivartate
english: Not all the Vedas, O descendant of Bharata, nor all the sacrifices, could achieve what he achieves who, having eaten flesh, thereafter turns away from it.

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ hi rasajñena māṃsasya parivarjanam cartuṃ vratam idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvaprāṇyabhayapradam
english: Hard indeed it is for one who has known its taste to abstain from flesh; yet to keep this most excellent vow is to grant freedom from fear to every living thing.

sanskrit: sarvabhūteṣu yo vidvān dadāty abhayadakṣiṇām dātā bhavati loke sa prāṇānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: The wise man who bestows upon all beings the gift of fearlessness becomes in the world a giver of life itself — herein is no doubt.

sanskrit: evaṃ vai paramaṃ dharmaṃ praśaṃsanti manīṣiṇaḥ prāṇā yathātmano 'bhīṣṭā bhūtānām api te tathā
english: Thus indeed do the wise extol this highest dharma: as life is dear to oneself, so too is it dear to all beings.

sanskrit: ātmaupamyena gantavyaṃ buddhimadbhir mahātmabhiḥ mṛtyuto bhayam astīti viduṣāṃ bhūtim icchatām
english: By measuring others against oneself should the wise and great-souled proceed, knowing that there is fear of death even for the learned who long for prosperity.

sanskrit: kiṃ punar hanyamānānāṃ tarasā jīvitārthinām arogāṇām apāpānāṃ pāpair māṃsopajīvibhiḥ
english: How much more, then, the terror of creatures violently slain — creatures that long to live, free of disease and free of sin — by the sinful who make their living on flesh!

sanskrit: tasmād viddhi mahārāja māṃsasya parivarjanam dharmasyāyatanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ svargasya ca sukhasya ca
english: Therefore know, O great king, that abstaining from flesh is the most excellent abode of dharma, and of heaven, and of happiness.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā paramo dharmas tathāhiṃsā paraṃ tapaḥ ahiṃsā paramaṃ satyaṃ tato dharmaḥ pravartate
english: Non-harming is the highest dharma; non-harming, likewise, is the highest austerity; non-harming is the highest truth, and from it dharma proceeds.

sanskrit: na hi māṃsaṃ tṛṇāt kāṣṭhād upalād vāpi jāyate hatvā jantuṃ tato māṃsaṃ tasmād doṣo 'sya bhakṣaṇe
english: For flesh is not born of grass, nor of wood, nor of stone; flesh comes only from the slaying of a creature, and therein lies the fault of eating it.

sanskrit: svāhāsvadhāmṛtabhujo devāḥ satyārjavapriyāḥ kravyādān rākṣasān viddhi jihmānṛtaparāyaṇān
english: The gods, who feed on the offerings of svāhā and svadhā and on the nectar of immortality, love truth and uprightness; but know the flesh-eating rākṣasas to be devoted to crookedness and falsehood.

sanskrit: kāntāreṣv atha ghoreṣu durgeṣu gahaneṣu ca rātrāv ahani saṃdhyāsu catvareṣu sabhāsu ca amāṃsabhakṣaṇe rājan bhayam ante na gacchati
english: In dreadful wildernesses, in fastnesses and dense thickets, by night and by day, at the twilights, at the crossroads and in the assembly halls — O king, for one who eats no flesh no fear comes at the last.
